hook.line: Sooner or later someone asks you for something you flatly will not do. A plain *no* is polite; *ni* makes the refusal land. In the café, Altamira keeps asking Tomás to sell.
hook.es: ¿Vender el café a Altamira? Ni pensarlo.
hook.en: Sell the café to Altamira? No way.

examples.es: ¿Vender el café a Altamira? Ni pensarlo.
examples.en: Sell the café to Altamira? No way.

examples.es: No me llamó ni siquiera para mi cumpleaños.
examples.en: He didn't even call me for my birthday.

examples.es:
¿Vas a bailar con Hernando?
Ni loca.
examples.en:
Are you going to dance with Hernando?
Not on your life. (a woman speaking)

examples.es:
¿Cerrar el café un domingo?
Ni hablar.
examples.en:
Close the café on a Sunday?
No way.

rule: *Ni* is a *no* with the volume turned up. Alone, it refuses: *ni pensarlo*, *ni hablar*, *ni loco* (a woman says *ni loca*). Before a noun it means "not even one": *ni una palabra*. *Ni siquiera* means "not even" and goes before the verb, or after it if the sentence already has *no*: *No me llamó ni siquiera para mi cumpleaños*. English says "not even" without a *no* in sight, so watch for it: once *ni* is there, Spanish wants the whole sentence negative.
smallPrint: Teachers call this the emphatic use of *ni*, a negative that strengthens the refusal.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *ni* or *no* to refuse flatly: *___ pensarlo.*
yourTurn.why: *Ni* is what turns a plain refusal into "no way".

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Not a word to anyone.
yourTurn.why: *Ni una* means "not even one", and *nadie* stays negative to match.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: She didn't even greet me.
yourTurn.why: *Ni siquiera* is "not even", placed before the verb.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: He didn't even offer me a coffee.
accept: No me ofreció ni un café.
yourTurn.why: *Ni un* before the noun means "not even one".

yourTurn.prompt: Make it stronger. Say: He didn't even call me for my birthday.
yourTurn.answer: No me llamó ni siquiera para mi cumpleaños.
accept: Ni siquiera me llamó para mi cumpleaños.

yourTurn.prompt: Refuse flatly, as a woman: Not on your life.
Type in Spanish: It isn't expensive, not by a long way.
yourTurn.answer: No es caro, ni mucho menos.
accept: No es caro ni mucho menos.
yourTurn.why: *Ni mucho menos* closes a *no* sentence with "not at all".

pitfalls.why: Almost. For a flat "no way", *ni* does the work, not *no*.
Almost. After *ni*, the sentence stays negative, so you need *nadie*, not *alguien*.

pitfalls.wrong: No me llamó siquiera para mi cumpleaños.
pitfalls.right: No me llamó ni siquiera para mi cumpleaños.
pitfalls.why: Almost. English "even" is not enough here; "not even" needs *ni siquiera*.
